comparison: Both address claims about GGN's biophysical capacity for graded transmission (C2, C21, C39-C41, C66). OpenEval finds these claims well-supported by computational modeling with biophysically plausible parameters. Peer reviewers rate these as UNCERTAIN, noting that prior experimental work (Papadopoulou et al., 2011) already demonstrated this capacity, questioning whether the model disambiguates alternative hypotheses.

Both evaluate claims about feedback inhibition expanding KC dynamic range (C42-C44). OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED by computational modeling with cross-species validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of experimental validation and stating 'The authors have not demonstrated that feedback inhibition expands the dynamic range of KCs' - this is a model prediction requiring clearer presentation.

OpenEval R2 addresses claims C3, C45 (among others) about GGN hyperpolarization responses. Peer R3 specifically evaluates C3 and C45, rating them SUPPORTED as 'novel functional properties' based on valid in vivo recording data. Both agree these experimental observations are well-founded.

Perfect claim overlap (C22, C46-C51) regarding heterogeneity requirements in the model. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by systematic modeling with biological constraints. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting limited exploration of parameter space - only testing all-active vs 1/5 inactive KCs, requesting more thorough testing of different KC input patterns.

Perfect claim overlap (C25, C52-C57) on high-firing KC subpopulation. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of model predictions with experimental data from 147 KCs. Peer reviewers accept the experimental validation but note consistency with prior literature (Perez-Orive et al., 2002), questioning novelty while accepting the finding.

OpenEval R2 includes claims C23-C24, C58-C65 about unknown excitatory pathway to inhibitory neurons. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED by timing analysis and silencing experiments. Peer R6 evaluates overlapping claims (C23-C24, C58-C65) as UNCERTAIN, noting contradictions in antennal nerve cutting experiments and alternative explanations (maxillary palps).

Perfect claim overlap (C26-C37) on GGN morphological characterization. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes detailed reconstruction with novel peduncle-wrapping neurites. Peer reviewers describe the anatomical characterization as 'a useful resource' and 'a valuable advance,' accepting the morphological findings without challenge.

High overlap on background claims about GGN (C1, C14-C19). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-established properties providing context. Peer reviewers accept these as foundational knowledge without challenge, treating them as established context for evaluating novel findings.

Perfect claim overlap (C4-C13) on olfactory system background. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes these as consensus knowledge providing necessary context. Peer reviewers accept these established background claims from prior literature without challenge.

OpenEval R1 includes biophysical parameters (C86-C89) used in modeling GGN transmission. Peer R10 evaluates these same parameters as SUPPORTED, noting reviewers asked for elaboration but accepted them as reasonable literature-based values for non-spiking neurons.

High overlap on comparative literature claims (C69-C75, C79-C81). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these accurately summarize Drosophila findings for comparative context. Peer reviewers find these literature comparisons valuable and do not challenge their accuracy, with one reviewer requesting more discussion of Inada et al., 2017.

OpenEval R4 includes cross-species validation claims (C76-C78) supporting dynamic range predictions. Peer R11 addresses broader literature context including these claims, rating them SUPPORTED as accurate citations that provide valuable comparative context.

OpenEval R10 addresses connectivity patterns and mathematical calculations (C83-C85) used as model constraints. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these technical details appear accepted implicitly as part of the modeling framework.
